title: The week's digest drops every conversation on a pitched Linga scene
body:
## Summary
rules/digest cleanEntry refused an english entry whose sceneId is a pitched scene id, so withDigest dropped every finished conversation on a pitched scene and the Sunday page never counted it.

## Description
cleanEntry accepted a scene id only from AUTHORED_SCENES or PLAN_ID (desk/src/lib/rules/digest.ts:58, :117). english/conversation.ts mints a third family, pitch- plus 8 hex (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:493), and writes it on finish (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:397); learners.withDigest drops an entry cleanEntry refuses without a log. Fixed: PITCH_ID beside PLAN_ID (desk/src/lib/rules/digest.ts:60); the page counts the conversation and never names it (its title is the learner's own).

## Flow
- Adult learner pitches a scene, talks, presses Finish
- endTake -> withDigest({sceneId:'pitch-xxxxxxxx'}) -> cleanEntry null -> nothing written
- Sunday page: no Linga section for that week
- Fix: accept /^pitch-[0-9a-f]{8}$/; the test mints an id with PITCH_PREFIX and checks 7 junk ids are still dropped

## Expected impact
Adult-mode learners see their pitched conversations counted on the week page. Could break: a malformed id slipping the whitelist; the test pins 7 junk ids.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every finished conversation reaches the week's record
Before: cleanEntry(pitch entry) = null; 1 of 3 minted scene-id families dropped
After: kept; page reads 'One conversation.' with no title; 7 junk ids still dropped
Method: gate - week-digest-test new case red (32/1) then green (33/33)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/rules/digest.ts:117 (before: SCENES.has || PLAN_ID.test)
desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:493 `${PITCH_PREFIX}${randomUUID().slice(0,8)}`
probe: cleanEntry({kind:'english',sceneId:'pitch-0a1b2c3d',...}) -> null

title: A Linga take finished with no reply counts as a conversation and an evening
body:
## Summary
The Sunday page counted an english digest entry with turns 0 as a conversation and an evening of work, while every other digest kind is on file only with a count above 0.

## Description
cleanEntry drops a maths set of 0 items, a reading of 0 sentences, a sheet of 0 problems and a paper of 0 questions, but keeps an english entry at turns 0 (desk/src/lib/rules/digest.ts:120). Finish is accepted in your-turn (desk/src/lib/english/turn.ts:69), so a scene opened and closed in silence wrote turns 0 (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:397) and rules/week said 'Mia worked on one evening. One conversation: Say that again, please.' Fixed read-side: sundayPage reads past a turns-0 english entry (desk/src/lib/rules/week.ts:215); no stored entry is rewritten.

## Flow
- Learner starts a Linga scene and presses Finish before replying
- digest gets {kind:'english',turns:0}
- parent page: one evening, one conversation, the scene named
- Fix: filter turns-0 english entries out of the page week; test alone, beside a real take, and with a phrase on file

## Expected impact
A parent no longer reads an evening of work that did not happen. Could break: nothing stored changes; the recap is separate.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the parent page counts only things done
Before: digest [teacher, turns 0] -> 5 lines, 1 evening, 1 conversation
After: 'Nothing this week.'; beside a real take 1 conversation, not 2
Method: gate - week-rules-test new case red (20/1) then green (21/21)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: zero kinds accepted: maths:false essay:false homework:false paper:false; english turns 0 -> kept
zero-reply take page: ['Mia worked on one evening.','# Linga','One conversation: Say that again, please.',...]

title: A scene name ending in a question mark closed the Linga line with '?.'
body:
## Summary
rules/week namesLine always appended a stop, so 'Speaking practice: what do you think?' read '...what do you think?.' on the parent page; the suite checked only 11 of the 17 authored scene names.

## Description
namesLine built `${head}: ${names}.` unconditionally (desk/src/lib/rules/week.ts:283). AUTHORED_SCENES is ENGLISH_SCENES plus SPEAKING_PRACTICE (desk/src/lib/english/curriculum.ts:82); tools/week-rules-test.cjs iterated ENGLISH_SCENES only. Fixed: a line already ending in . ! or ? takes no second stop (desk/src/lib/rules/week.ts:287); the test walks all 17 and a plan title ending in '?'.

## Flow
- Learner finishes the sp-what-do-you-think scene
- Sunday page Linga line: 'One conversation: Speaking practice: what do you think?.'
- Fix: test over AUTHORED_SCENES, then the stop rule

## Expected impact
A parent reads clean punctuation on every scene. Could break: a name ending in a stop the page meant to add; pinned for all 17.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one sentence, one stop on every Linga line
Before: 1 of 17 authored names gives '?.'; 6 of 17 unchecked
After: 0 of 17; 17 of 17 checked within LINE_WORDS
Method: gate - week-rules-test new case red (21/1) then green (22/22)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: sp-what-do-you-think -> One conversation: Speaking practice: what do you think?.
AUTHORED_SCENES 17, ENGLISH_SCENES 11

title: The look line was checked for 14 of 53 unit slips
body:
## Summary
The Sunday page's slip line has no trim rung, yet the suite drew only each unit's first slip, so a long name on any of the other 39 would pass the suite and overflow LINE_WORDS.

## Description
'The most common slip, <n>: <name>.' (desk/src/lib/rules/week.ts) leaves eight words for the name; test 6 used SCHOOL_UNIT_SLIPS[unit][0] (tools/week-rules-test.cjs). The new case walks every slip of every unit (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:3703) at 2, 3 and 12 times.

## Flow
- Seed a 9-word name on range-backwards in memory (node -r)
- HEAD suite: green 22/22
- new suite: red; unseeded green 23/23

## Expected impact
A future slip name that breaks the page is caught by the gate. Could break: nothing; test only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the gate sees every slip the page can name
Before: 14 of 53 unit slips checked; a seeded 9-word name passes
After: 53 of 53 (159 lines); the seed fails
Method: gate - seeded control red under the new case, green under HEAD
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
seed-before (HEAD suite + seed): pass 22 fail 0
seed-after (new suite + seed): pass 22 fail 1
unit slip ids 53, first-of-unit 14

title: The no-count guard read a typed list of three collection screens
body:

## Description

## Evaluation

title: The habit detectors' header claimed two readers that are not built
body:
## Summary
rules/habits.ts said in the present tense that the twin plants and checks a habit (D6) and a Sitting proves a rule (D7); no module imports the file and the Sitting is not started.

## Description

After: 0 false claims

title: The Sunday page capture claimed a 44 px tap-target check it never asserts
body:
## Summary
tools/sunday-page-live.cjs said it asserts the Recap tab's buttons are at least 44 px tall; it only records them in report.json.

## Description
layout() collects `short` targets; the run writes them to report.json and no assert reads them (tools/sunday-page-live.cjs). The plan notes the 26 px Student/Parent toggle as pre-existing. Header corrected.

## Flow
- Operator runs the capture, it passes
- Reads the header as a 44 px pass
- report.json lists short targets

## Expected impact
An operator does not take a green capture as a tap-target pass. Could break: nothing; comment only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the capture says what it checks
Before: 1 claimed assertion, 0 asserts on short
After: header matches code
Method: probe - read of the asserts; node --check exit 0 (the live run is the operator's)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/sunday-page-live.cjs: short computed in layout(), only used in report[p.id] = { ..., short: lay.short }

title: Essay TV reads the raw stored mode while the essay reading reads modeOf
body:
## Summary
rules/essay adultSeat is `profile.mode === 'adult'`, bypassing rules/mode modeOf; it disagrees with modeOf on 59 of 180 profile rows, so the Essay TV speaks school words to a derived adult and adult words to a minor with a stored adult.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/essay.ts:979 reads the stored field; api/analyse passes modeOf to the reading (desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:109). mode.ts says no audience decision bypasses modeOf and a stored adult is honoured only behind the 18+ gate (desk/src/lib/rules/mode.ts:21). A 19-year-old with no stored mode is Adult by modeOf (collect-rules-test pins it) but adultSeat is false: the TV says 'one paragraph' while the reading calls them 'an adult writer'. A hand-edited stored adult on a 12-year-old makes adultSeat true. Technique: invariant-placement/placement-precedes-gate (one door, then a gate on raw reads). Fix: adultSeat = modeOf(seated, prefs) === 'adult'.

## Flow
- Seat a 19-year-old high-school profile, no stored mode
- Essay home caption: 'Paste ... one paragraph' (school) while the reading names an adult writer
- Fix: route adultSeat through modeOf; add the 180-row grid test plus a source scan for raw .mode === 'adult' reads outside rules/mode and store modeChecked

## Expected impact
Adults see the adult Essay chrome; minors never do. Could break: EssayTV captions for unset-mode adults change (tv-keys/essay pins).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one mode decision on every Essay surface
Before: adultSeat vs modeOf disagree on 59/180 grid rows
After: 0/180
Method: probe - the grid run against both functions; the fix lies in rules/essay.ts (desk-pipelines context)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: grid 180 disagree 59; e.g. {type:'elementary',mode:'adult',modeOf:false,adultSeat:true}
desk/src/lib/rules/essay.ts:979 export const adultSeat = (s: Seat) => seatedProfile(s)?.mode === 'adult';
instrument: tools/mode-rules-test.cjs grid: adultSeat(seat(p)) === (modeOf(p,prefs)==='adult') over 10 ages x 3 types x 3 modes x 2 boxes, plus the essay suites (essay-seat-test) on the change; out-of-scope: rules/essay.ts belongs to desk-pipelines

title: Two Linga prompts describe a Family-mode 'other' learner differently
body:
## Summary
english/check.ts calls a stored-Family 'other' learner with no age 'an adult in Family mode'; english/conversation.ts, reading isAdult, calls the same learner 'of unspecified age ... children' and 'not an adult'.

## Description
desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:43 tests p.mode === 'family' && adultAllowed(p); desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:137 and :144 test isAdult(p, prefs). For type other, no age, Linga box unticked, stored family, the first is true and the second false (1 of 60 Family-mode rows). mode.ts says no audience decision calls isAdult directly (desk/src/lib/rules/mode.ts:58). Fix: one helper in rules/mode (e.g. adultInFamily(p, prefs)) both prompts read.

## Flow
- Profile: type other, no age, Mode Family, box unticked
- Placement check prompt: 'an adult in Family mode'
- Conversation prompt: 'of unspecified age; keep every exchange appropriate for children' and 'This learner is not an adult.'

## Expected impact
One learner is described one way to every Linga model call. Could break: prompts on the live surface change for that row; a drift record is owed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one description of a learner across Linga prompts
Before: 1 of 60 Family-mode profile rows described two ways
After: 0 of 60
Method: probe - the 60-row grid of isAdult vs adultAllowed under a stored family
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: family-mode adult wording grid 60 disagree 1 {type:'other',c:false,conversation:false,check:true}
instrument: a rules/mode helper plus a test asserting check.ts and conversation.ts produce the same audience words over the 60-row grid (stub the text provider and read both systems); out-of-scope (english context) and live surface: drift record owed

title: The tutor voice calls an adult a teenager on Linga and a 15-year-old on essay hints
body:
## Summary
rules/voice names a known-age learner only in maths: voiceOf('english', 46) is 'a Czech teenager' and voiceOf('essay', 46) is 'a 15-year-old', and no voiceOf call reads the Adult mode, while the essay reading says 'an adult writer'.

## Description
TEEN is a fixed table (desk/src/lib/rules/voice.ts:70); voiceOf names an age for maths only (desk/src/lib/rules/voice.ts:83); essayReadingVoice alone takes the mode (desk/src/lib/rules/voice.ts:97). Callers without the mode: desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:156, desk/src/lib/desk/explain.ts:118, desk/src/lib/desk/worked.ts:45, desk/src/lib/desk/english.ts:16. An Adult-mode 'other' with no age gets 'a maths tutor for a 15-year-old'. Fix: voiceOf takes the mode and names an adult as essayReadingVoice does; english and essay name a known age; the four callers pass the mode.

## Flow
- Seat helena-46 (Adult, age 46)
- Linga caption prompt: 'talking to a Czech teenager'; essay hint: 'a writing tutor for a 15-year-old'
- Fix in voice.ts, callers pass modeOf; voice-rules-test pins the new rows

## Expected impact
Adults are addressed as adults by every engine prompt. Could break: byte-for-byte teen prompts at 14+ (voice-rules-test test 3) change on purpose; live surface, drift record owed.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the tutor names the learner it is speaking to
Before: ages 18-99 known: english 'teenager' 82/82, essay hint '15-year-old' 82/82; Adult with no age: 4 of 5 voices say teen
After: 0 of 82; Adult named as adult on all 5
Method: simulation - voiceOf/essayReadingVoice walked at ages 18, 30, 46 and none; the model-side effect needs the live drift record
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: age 46 maths: a 46-year-old | essay hint: a 15-year-old | english: a Czech teenager | reading adult: an adult writer
age undefined maths: a 15-year-old | essay hint: a 15-year-old | english: a Czech teenager
instrument: voice-rules-test rows over ages 14-99 x subjects x modes asserting no 'teenager'/'15-year-old' for 18+ or Adult, plus a live model-drift record (scripts/model-drift.ps1, the operator's) since hint/explain/english prompts change

title: The collection shelf reorders whenever an earned topic is practised again
body:
## Summary
rules/collect sorts collectibles by the record's lastSeen, which every attempt moves, so an earned lamp jumps to the right end each time its topic is practised; the header promises a shelf that grows rightwards.

## Description
byAge sorts by lastSeen (desk/src/lib/rules/collect.ts:38); recordAttempt sets lastSeen: Date.now() (desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:413); the header says 'oldest first ... the shelf grows rightwards' (desk/src/lib/rules/collect.ts:36). English keys follow insertion order, not age. The order a shelf needs is the latch time, which SkillRecord does not keep. Fix: a securedAt (and stretch.securedAt) set once when the latch flips, collectibles sorted by it (learners.ts is out of this round's paths).

## Flow
- Earn frac-equivalent (6 right), then area (6 right): shelf frac-equivalent, area
- One more attempt on frac-equivalent
- Shelf: area, frac-equivalent

## Expected impact
A child's shelf stays where they built it. Could break: old records with no securedAt need a fallback (lastSeen).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an earned object keeps its place
Before: one extra attempt reorders the shelf (probe: 2 of 2 lamps swap)
After: the shelf order is unchanged by practice
Method: probe - recordAttempt on a scratch DESK_DATA_DIR with a stepped clock
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: earned A then B: frac-equivalent,area
after one more A attempt: area,frac-equivalent
instrument: collect-rules-test case: earn A, earn B, practise A again, assert order [A, B]; needs securedAt on SkillRecord in lib/session/learners.ts (out-of-scope)

title: The digest cap is a count, so a busy week loses its first evening
body:
## Summary
cleanDigest keeps the last 60 entries whatever their age, so a week averaging 10 things a day drops its first day and the Sunday page says six evenings for seven.

## Description
DIGEST_CAP = 60 (desk/src/lib/rules/digest.ts:53) is applied by count (desk/src/lib/rules/digest.ts:150); the page reads seven days (desk/src/lib/rules/week.ts:213). The comment says sixty is 'weeks of evenings'; that holds at up to 8.5 entries a day. Fix: keep the last DIGEST_CAP entries or every entry within eight days of the newest, whichever is more.

## Flow
- A learner does 10 marked sets, readings and conversations a day for a week (70 entries)
- cleanDigest keeps 60: day one is gone
- Page: 'worked on six evenings'

## Expected impact
Exam-week heavy users get a true count. Could break: the learner file grows by at most a week of entries.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the page reads the whole week at any volume
Before: page exact up to 60 entries a week; at 10 a day it says 6 of 7 evenings
After: 7 of 7 at any volume
Method: probe - 8, 9, 10, 11 a day through cleanDigest + sundayPage
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: 8 a day -> evenings 7; 9 a day -> 7 (sets 60 of 63); 10 a day -> evenings 6; 11 a day -> 6
instrument: week-digest-test case seeding 10 entries a day for 7 days through learners.withDigest and asserting the page reads 7 evenings; the cap rule is in digest.ts but the write path is learners.ts (out-of-scope), so a worker owning both builds it

title: A step-up slip never reaches the parent's 'one thing to look at'
body:
## Summary
The digest keeps a set's slip only from the unit's usual list, so a step-up (top-rung) slip the TV names and the next step-up set aims at is dropped from the week.

## Description
knownSlip reads SCHOOL_UNIT_SLIPS only (desk/src/lib/rules/digest.ts:75); SCHOOL_TOP_SLIPS (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:3726) are named on top-rung items and aimed at by the next step-up set (desk/src/app/api/practice/route.ts:47). A pct-change step-up set with 'Took the percent of the new amount' on two items writes no slip. MB-B20 kept them off the unit list for the explain prompt, the aimed set and the ruler; the parent page is not named in that decision.

## Flow
- Step-up set on pct-change, two items wrong with pct-of-new
- mathsEntry: no slip
- Sunday page: no look line

## Expected impact
Whether a step-up slip is a parent's 'thing to look at' is a product call: the page may stay usual-only by design.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the parent sees the week's most frequent code-detected slip
Before: mathsEntry(pct-change, 2 x pct-of-new, stretch) -> no slip
After: slip pct-of-new, slipN 2, a look line when twice
Method: probe - mathsEntry on the sample
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: An Adult-mode learner is shown the parent's Sunday page
body:
## Summary
weekOf builds the parent's page for any seated learner and the phone draws it, so an adult reads 'One thing to try together: Ask them to teach you...' about themselves; the Adult plan's E4 ('no parent view at 18+') is unbuilt.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts weekOf has no mode check; desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:910 draws <WeekPage> for any seated learner; DO_IT and DO_IT_ELSE address a parent ('ask them') (desk/src/lib/rules/week.ts). docs/concepts/ADULT-MODE-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md E4 plans 'a week page on the phone from history lines; no parent view at 18+', Done unchecked.

## Flow
- Seat an Adult-mode learner (type other, Adult)
- Phone > Parent > Recap: 'This week' with parent acts
- E4: what the adult sees instead is undesigned

## Expected impact
Adults get a page written to them, not to a parent. Could break: the phone's Parent tab for adults.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the week page speaks to its reader
Before: Adult-mode seat: the parent page with 1 parent act ('Ask them ...')
After: an adult week page or none (E4)
Method: simulation - weekOf walked for an Adult profile; what replaces it is the owner's design (E4)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
docs/concepts/ADULT-MODE-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:423-424 E4 ... 'no parent view at 18+. Done: [ ] gate [ ] captures.'
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:910 <WeekPage lines={s.learner ? s.week : null} />
